card.title: Undo with reset
card.blurb: Move your branch back one commit and say where its files should land. Run `--soft`, `--mixed` and `--hard` on the same mistake and watch the three zones answer differently.
hero.title: Undo with reset
intro.0: The commit is made and it should not have been. Deleting the file and starting over is the tempting move, and it usually throws away more than the mistake. `reset` moves your branch's name back instead, and hands you the real decision: keep those files staged, drop them back in the folder, or let them go. Here you run all three on the same mistake and watch the zones answer.
task.1.title: Undo the commit, keep the work ready
task.1.context:
The commit on top is a mistake: `draft.txt` went in before it was ready, under the message `oops`.

`git reset <mode> <rev>` moves `main` back to the commit you name, and the mode decides where that file lands. Here you want it kept staged, ready to commit again the moment it is finished.
task.1.goal.0: Read `git log --oneline` and see how far back `add dog` is.
task.1.goal.1: Move `main` onto `add dog` with one `git reset`.
task.1.goal.2: `draft.txt` should end up staged, ready to go straight back in.
task.1.goal.3: Read `git diff --staged` - it prints the lines that commit was holding, still there.
task.2.title: Put the file back in the folder instead
task.2.context:
Same mistake, a different wish. This time you are not sure `draft.txt` belongs in the next commit either, and you want to choose again before anything is saved.

The move back is the same one; only the mode changes. Pick the mode that empties the staging area and drops the file in the working tree.
task.2.goal.0: Read `git log --oneline` and count back to `add dog` again.
task.2.goal.1: Move `main` there with a `git reset` that leaves nothing staged.
task.2.goal.2: `draft.txt` should sit in the working tree when you are done.
task.3.title: Drop the commit and its file
task.3.context:
This time `draft.txt` was never wanted. One of the three modes makes the same move back and keeps nothing: staging is emptied and the file goes from the folder as well.

It is the only one that throws work away, so read it twice before you run it. If you ever run it by mistake, `git reflog` still lists the commit you left behind for a while, and you can go back to it.
task.3.goal.0: Read `git log --oneline` and count back to `add dog` one more time.
task.3.goal.1: Move `main` there and keep nothing - nothing staged, and no `draft.txt` in the folder.
task.3.goal.2: `git status` should show nothing waiting in either zone.
task.4.title: Undo with reset - recap
task.4.context: One move back, three places for the files to land.
task.4.summaryIntro: Every reset did the same thing to the history: it moved the name you are standing on to the commit you named. The mode was never about the graph - it answered a second question, about the files that commit was holding.
task.4.summaryItems.0.title: `git reset --soft HEAD~1` -
task.4.summaryItems.0.text: moves the name back and leaves the files staged, ready to commit again.
task.4.summaryItems.1.title: `git reset --mixed HEAD~1` -
task.4.summaryItems.1.text: moves the name back and drops the files in the working tree, so you pick again.
task.4.summaryItems.2.title: `git reset --hard HEAD~1` -
task.4.summaryItems.2.text: moves the name back and keeps nothing; the files go with the commit.
task.4.summaryItems.3.title: `HEAD~1` -
task.4.summaryItems.3.text: one step back from where you stand, so you never have to copy a hash to undo.
task.4.summaryClose: That is most of the track: save work, split it, bring it back together, and move the labels when you get it wrong. One lesson left, on the other way of bringing two branches together.
